title: Team/Organization/User/Project model relationships
answers: How do Team, Organization and User relate?
body:
- `posthog/models/organization.py:Organization` top-level tenant; `members` M2M to `posthog.User` through `organization.py:OrganizationMembership` (level, joined_at, invited_by).
- `posthog/models/project.py:Project` FK to Organization (related_name `projects`); Project id == Team id.
- `posthog/models/team/team.py:Team` FKs: `organization` (related_name `teams`), `project` (related_name `teams`), `parent_team` (related_name `child_teams`, environments under a project).
- `posthog/models/user.py:User` (custom AbstractUser, UserManager) is not owned by one org; role comes from membership level. `current_organization`/`current_team` are UI preferences, not scoping defaults.
- `posthog/models/utils.py:RootTeamMixin` resolves child team to parent team for project-scoped data.

search: PostHog's core model hierarchy chains Organization → Project ↔ Team → User memberships with specific FK and M2M paths. Organization (posthog/models/organization.py) is the top-level tenant with M2M to User via OrganizationMembership (level, joined_at, invited_by); Project (posthog/models/project.py) is FK'd to Organization (related_name `projects`); Team (posthog/models/team/team.py) has FK to organization and project with child_teams under parent_team for environment scoping. User (posthog/models/user.py, custom AbstractUser) is not owned by a single org; role derives from OrganizationMembership level. RootTeamMixin (posthog/models/utils.py) resolves child teams to parent for project-scoped data queries.
